clearing.title: Industrial Clearing Convention
clearing.target: SOV or its actual recognised successor
clearing.basis: Continuity of inter-republic contracts, bilateral clearing and the trade-payment problems of the early transition.

technical.title: Technical Cooperation Convention
technical.basis: Technical licensing, training and enterprise restructuring partnerships. This is an alternate-history treaty based on those practices.

border.title: Border Administration Convention
border.basis: Successor-state border and customs administration. No settlement of a disputed border or third-country rights without consent.

training.title: Defence Training Convention
training.basis: Bilateral training missions and successor-state defence cooperation. This is a practical convention, not automatic collective security.

energy.title: Energy Transit Convention
energy.target: Selected eligible supplier or transit neighbour
energy.basis: Post-Soviet fuel supply and transit interdependence. No energy units, resource deposits or pipelines are created by this administrative agreement.

water.title: Shared Basin Convention
water.target: Selected RP country sharing the actual basin
water.basis: The 1992 Almaty water-cooperation agreement and earlier shared irrigation management provide a later historical analogue. Earlier agreements are alternate history.

romanian.title: Romanian Cultural Convention
romanian.basis: Romanian-Moldavian linguistic and cultural links. This alternate-history convention has no territorial reward.

external.title: Gosplan Directives
external.description: The planning committee no longer asks: it directs. Special tasks for single republics become routine.

external.title: The People's Control
external.description: Committees of People's Control in every ministry and every kolkhoz check the figures the republics report.

external.title: Party Commission
external.description: Pelshe's commission punishes on behalf of the Party itself - and the Party does not need to explain itself to the republics.

external.title: Socialist Emulation
external.description: Republic against republic, factory against factory: the best of the plan carry the Transferable Red Banner.

shock.name: Shock Therapy
shock.description: Prices, trade and enterprise privileges will be released in a single programme. New firms and investment can respond quickly to genuine demand, but wages, savings and public revenue will bear the disruption before a new commercial order is secure.

gradual.name: Gradual Transition
gradual.description: Essential prices and public commitments will change in stages while enterprises acquire new customers and commercial accounts. The government will preserve a measure of household security, accepting slower investment and a continuing obligation to support weak producers.

directed.name: Directed Reconstruction
directed.description: The state will retain command of strategic enterprises and finance their reconstruction through a national investment plan. Public control can protect jobs and essential supply, but the treasury must carry risks that a private investor would refuse.

auction.title: Competitive Sale
auction.description: A public auction will invite investors to acquire the enterprise with clear obligations and published accounts. The state gains modest proceeds and new management, while accepting a smaller immediate share of the firm's income and the risk of restructuring its workforce.

workers.title: Worker Buyout
workers.description: Employees and local investors will acquire the enterprise through a supervised buyout. The settlement protects workplace knowledge and social confidence, but limited capital and concessional financing leave more of the initial burden with the public budget.

liquidate.title: Close the Combine
liquidate.description: An unviable enterprise will be closed and its recoverable assets sold. The decision ends a claim on scarce public resources and clears the way for new activity, while destroying productive capacity and leaving the workforce to find a new livelihood.

public.title: Public Retooling
public.description: The enterprise will remain in public ownership while its equipment, management and accounts are reorganised. The state preserves productive capacity and employment, taking responsibility for an investment whose return depends on finding viable customers.

sectors: Consumer workshops and light manufacturing employ workers whose skills may not find an immediate place in larger industrial combines.
Processing plants connect rural producers to urban consumers. Their reconstruction must preserve viable agricultural supply as well as factory machinery.
Repair workshops keep machinery working across the economy. Their customers and staff may be worth more than the equipment listed in a hurried valuation.
Construction depends on a reliable supply of materials. New owners can improve production, but a poorly handled sale can interrupt the wider building economy.
Factories producing household goods need new designs, distribution and customers. Their workers face a demanding transition from guaranteed orders to competitive sales.
Specialised suppliers were organised around larger Union customers. Some can find new orders; others survive only through arrears and public support.

The settlement protects workplace knowledge and social confidence, but limited capital and concessional financing leave more of the initial burden with the public budget.

decisions.title: Light Industry: Close the Combine
decisions.description: Consumer workshops and light manufacturing employ workers whose skills may not find an immediate place in larger industrial combines. An unviable enterprise will be closed and its recoverable assets sold. The decision ends a claim on scarce public resources and clears the way for new activity, while destroying productive capacity and leaving the workforce to find a new livelihood.

decisions.title: Light Industry: Public Retooling
decisions.description: Consumer workshops and light manufacturing employ workers whose skills may not find an immediate place in larger industrial combines. The enterprise will remain in public ownership while its equipment, management and accounts are reorganised. The state preserves productive capacity and employment, taking responsibility for an investment whose return depends on finding viable customers.

decisions.title: Food Processing: Competitive Sale

rules.prices: Every fee, receipt and recurring allocation is a specified share of the relevant country's GDP. Setup shares use GDP at execution. Weekly shares use current GDP at each weekly pass. No fixed dollar price is used.
rules.window: The first sovereign reform course starts its 730-day window once. The same country cannot restart or extend it by changing government, rejoining the Union, repeating a decision or saving and loading. The absolute deadline survives suspension. Timed benefits and fiscal burdens require actual independence.
rules.growth: productivity_growth_modifier is a number input. At neutral scalars +1.2 produces +0.6 state productivity points per monthly pass, approximately +14.4 over 24 passes. State catch-up and other native modifiers change the actual result. It is not +120 percent annual growth.
rules.consumer_goods: consumer_goods_factor is relative to the native corporate-tax-derived consumer-goods base. +18 percent is not eighteen percentage points of all factories. The burden is a game abstraction for industrial capacity tied up in restructuring, distinct from the fiscal loss.
rules.finite: There are six sector lots. Each lot can be settled once by one method, and only one lot can be in progress nationally. The chosen method consumes the same lot receipt; government changes cannot reopen it. A shared 30-day interval follows completion.
rules.relief: Each settled lot removes one sixth of this reform course's original restructuring burden: 3 percentage points of the modifier for shock, 1.5 for gradual, 1 for directed reconstruction. Six lots remove that spirit. Changes never lower unrelated consumer-goods requirements. Settlement modifiers belong to the national restructuring programme and persist through party changes while independent.
rules.capacity: A competitive sale or worker buyout preserves CIVs. Liquidation removes one actual industrial_complex level in the selected owned and controlled core state and requires at least two levels there at execution. Removed capacity, GDP and tax consequences use the native economy. No factory destruction is disguised as an ownership transfer.
rules.authority: Competitive sales and worker buyouts require the market-property charter from the chosen independent political programme. Public retooling requires its public-investment charter. Liquidation remains available under any sovereign government. The country must have an eligible surviving enterprise; no sector is a licence to remove a foreign state's factory.
rules.transaction: The fee, proceeds, factory removal if any, named programme changes and lot receipt execute atomically after current sovereignty, authority, ownership and control are rechecked. Failed or cancelled execution produces no payment, proceeds or receipt. Progress restoration grants no repeated proceeds or modifiers.

rules.status: Proposed implementation contract, not an existing SSR API
rules.ssr: IMP_is_1970_scenario and COLDWAR_SOV_is_union_republic and a recorded scenario SSR identity or a subsequently accepted SSR admission. A whitelisted puppet by itself is insufficient.
rules.sovereign: Existing state exists, is not a subject of any country, and has a recorded actual SSR independence or Union dissolution transition. A successful unilateral secession can create that record as well as a negotiated release; continuing Soviet approval is not a requirement for independent domestic content. Occupation or a different overlord does not count as independence.
rules.transition: Apply once on that real status transition. Do not release countries, change government, create borders or transfer units from focus completion. Re-entry to the USSR suspends the aftermath; a second exit resumes the stored recovery state without repeated rewards.
rules.programme: Sector rewards modify one named dynamic programme for that sector. One primary Union specialisation may be selected from nine mutually exclusive roles. All shared SSR content requires recognised SSR status without a communist-party or Soviet-outlook gate. Ordinary Union-dependent programmes suspend on independence. The chosen specialisation instead becomes a national legacy: 20 percent of beneficial modifiers and scoped equipment bonuses, 75 percent of adverse modifiers, and half the weekly GDP maintenance share. Construction, research bonuses and earned experience remain national assets. Each independent party has one stored programme requiring actual sovereignty and the exact current slot; departure suspends that programme and return never repeats one-time rewards.
rules.durable: Construction, earned experience, limited research bonuses and completed civil registers are national gains. Removal or replacement of an inherited problem is a persistent reform receipt, separate from a party programme. Existing infrastructure and state institutions survive a government change.
rules.starting: The Union Technical Network ends with genuine SSR status or suspended Union links. Plan shortages and patronage persist unless actually reformed. The original or reformed Social Guarantees persist after independence until a separately designed welfare reform changes them. Regional constraints persist in original or managed form.
rules.recovery: Each of supply, state accounts and defence administration has three distinct repairs. Count unique completed repair receipts, independently of completion order. One leaves two thirds of the initial penalty, two leave one third, three remove it. State accounts can be repaired across different chapters in either order; a later focus never restores an earlier penalty. Both exclusive budget courses provide the same third distinct receipt. Actual completed preparations reduce only their specified initial liability. Negotiated separation reduces the remaining liability to 60 percent only if a real accepted settlement keeps deliveries, payments and administration operating. Continued war or interrupted terms invalidate that mitigation until restored; elapsed time alone repairs nothing.
rules.exposure: Union Supply Contracts gives the stated SSR reward and adds Unconverted Union Orders on independence. Export Conversion or Domestic Suppliers removes that separate penalty. Diversify Orders is mutually exclusive and reduces the starting supply liability instead. These ordinary contracts are distinct from the nine mutually exclusive primary specialisations.
rules.bilateral: Each concrete foreign-policy focus dispatches one offer to one eligible named RP recipient, selected through its completion event. The recipient receives Accept and Refuse decisions with the complete two-country effects. Setup costs occur only on acceptance, once. Refusal charges neither country and opens a 180-day renegotiation decision for the same terms. Each originating republic has one active or pending partner per contract type. A shared recipient programme and its weekly operating budget apply once per contract type while any valid pair remains active; accepting additional republics does not multiply its national modifiers. The actual marginal preview must reflect any already active recipient programme. Acceptance rechecks status, geography, prerequisites and restrictions.
rules.standing: Signatures have no expiry. Both states must exist, remain at peace with each other, impose no native embargo and none of the four mirrored Imperia diplomatic, financial, economic or military sanctions in either direction. Failure suspends that pair's entitlements, spirits and dedicated weekly expenses. A shared recipient programme remains only if another valid signed pair independently supports it, and never multiplies its national modifiers. Restoration resumes the actual active programmes without fees or one-time rewards. Either signatory may terminate. Recognition of one actual Soviet successor is recorded by the dissolution settlement, not inferred from an arbitrary tag.
rules.geography: Border commissions require an actual land neighbour. Water commissions require a shared real basin. Energy transit requires an actual supplier-route relationship. Technical and training treaties require the partner capability recorded in the agreement. These focuses remain inspectable when ineligible. A focus with no live eligible counterpart stays unavailable and cannot block unrelated regional diplomacy.
rules.no_duplicate: No duplicate subject subsidy, ministry system, COMECON treaty membership, automatic army, free uranium deposit or automatic conflict. SSRs retain existing COMECON access. The 1985 autonomy penalties are not assumed to exist in the 1970 start.
rules.equipment: Equipment production costs use native idea equipment_bonus entries with build_cost_ic and instant = yes. The six weapon-related specialisations also retain their original military output, efficiency-cap or dockyard modifiers where present. Explicit equipment targets cover the intended class; no unstated parent-to-duplicate inheritance is assumed. Completed components accumulate once in the active programme and are replaced by their separately scaled legacy on independence. Distinct archetypes remain distinct named rows, never repeated under the same target. Existing MD native names are used in every preview. Designer and non-designer application and existing-variant refresh require an in-game check.
